resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (current application titled Certificate of Resale)
requirements: Grass cut, no snow or ice, and no trash or debris on the property, or the inspection is cancelled
Violations found at the first inspection are mailed within 2 weeks and must be fixed within 30 days of the letter; call to schedule a re-inspection
Open permits for the property must be dealt with before the certificate is issued
Smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors, fire extinguishers, oil tanks, grass and weeds, and litter or debris cannot be deferred to the buyer by affidavit
No one may live in the basement
If there is a third floor or full attic, the buyer's affidavit must state it will not be used as a separate unit or dwelling area (unless the attic is big enough and has proper egress)
A smoke certificate from the Fire Department is also required
Bulk trash is limited to three items a week; larger cleanouts need a private hauler and a dumpster permit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Resale application and pay by check or money order payable to Township of Hillside at the Building Department, 1409 Liberty Avenue. Then call (973) 926-5100 to set the inspection date; inspection request forms can be emailed to inspectionrequests@hillsidenj.us. The certificate is mailed to the applicant after approval (no pick-up, fax or copies). A buyer who takes on the repairs may file an Affidavit of Compliance promising to fix them within 30 days of closing, subject to the Construction Official's approval.

resale_co.notes: The Building and Housing page still calls it a Certificate of Continued Occupancy; the application posted September 2026 is titled Certificate of Resale with the same fees as the February 2026 Certificate of Continued Occupancy form. Commercial or industrial: $400 new owner, $300 change of tenant. The 2020 rules sheet attaches a 2005 state memo on fire extinguishers; the state dropped the extinguisher from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), but the Township rules still list fire extinguishers among items that cannot be deferred, so confirm. Rental-only items: a Certificate of Habitability is required to rent residential units, plus landlord registration and vacant property registration; these are not resale requirements. On the Township pages some displayed emails do not match the underlying mailto links (for example the Fire Subcode Official's shown address galeu@hillsidenj.us links to gfalkman@hillsidenj.us); the displayed addresses are used.

requirements: Township rules list smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers as items the seller must complete before the Certificate of Continued Occupancy (they cannot be deferred to the buyer)

fire_cert.notes: No Hillside smoke/CO certificate fee schedule, form or lead time was found on the Township site or the Fire Department's own website (hillsidefire.org, last updated around 2007). A search tool summary mentioned $150 / $250 / $375 tiers and 180-day validity, but the source could not be confirmed as Hillside's, so no fee is recorded. other_items.label: Open permits
